title: Cofinal coefficient quotient cocone with its completed projections
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$, a chosen uniformizer $\pi$, a unit $u\in O^\times$ and an integer $e\geq1$ such that $\ell=u\pi^e$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be any scheme and on its small pro-étale site put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$, $B_N=(O/\ell^N)_T$, $D_j=(O/\pi^j)_T$ for positive integers $N,j$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Let $\beta_N:R\to B_N$ and $\delta_j:R\to D_j$ be the canonical projections under the completed coefficient inverse-limit identifications of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Write $b_{N,M}:B_N\to B_M$ and $d_{j,k}:D_j\to D_k$ for reduction when $N\geq M$ and $j\geq k$.

For every $eN\geq j$ the inclusion $(\ell^N)\subseteq(\pi^j)$ induces a surjective ring-sheaf map $q_{N,j}:B_N\to D_j$, induced by $x\bmod\ell^N\mapsto x\bmod\pi^j$, satisfying
$$q_{N,j}\beta_N=\delta_j.$$
For $N\geq M$, $eM\geq j$, and $j\geq k\geq1$, the following are equalities of the actual ring-sheaf maps:
$$q_{M,j}b_{N,M}=q_{N,j},\qquad d_{j,k}q_{N,j}=q_{N,k}.$$
Thus these maps, including the completed projections, form one commuting quotient diagram, with identity and composite reductions included. The source and target finite rings of $q_{N,j}$ are finite commutative rings annihilated by $\ell^N$. These assertions hold for arbitrary ramification and arbitrary $T$, with no invertibility assumption on $\ell$.

proof.text: Since $u^N$ is a unit, $(\ell^N)=(\pi^{eN})\subseteq(\pi^j)$ when $eN\geq j$. Thus $f_{N,j}:O/(\ell^N)\to O/(\pi^j)$, $[x]\mapsto[x]$, is well defined: changing $x$ by $\ell^Na$ changes it by $\pi^j(u^N\pi^{eN-j}a)$. It preserves addition, multiplication and one, and every target class has a representative $x\in O$, so it is surjective. Clause (4) of the coefficient-extension datum gives finiteness of $O/(\pi^j)$ and of $O/(\pi^{eN})=O/(\ell^N)$, since $j,eN\geq1$. Multiplication by $\ell^N$ is zero on both quotients, because $\ell^N$ belongs to both defining ideals.

proof.text: Apply ring-valued constant sheafification to $f_{N,j}$ to obtain the actual map $q_{N,j}:B_N\to D_j$. The universal property of sheafification defines this functor on maps and preserves identities and composition by uniqueness. To check surjectivity, choose a section $s$ of the underlying surjective set map $f_{N,j}$, so $f_{N,j}s=\mathrm{id}$. Sheafify these set maps. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] the resulting source and target are the underlying sets of $B_N,D_j$; their map agrees with the underlying map of $q_{N,j}$ by the universal property, since both agree on constant labels. Consequently that underlying map has the sheafified $s$ as a right inverse. In particular $q_{N,j}$ is surjective on sections over every site object. The section is used only as a set map; no ring section is asserted. With independent site and coefficient universes, construct the forgetful-preserves-sheafification instance on a small model in the coefficient-sheaf universe, then transport it back along the equivalence of sites. This is Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.PreservesSheafification.transport and does not alter either universe.

proof.text: The constant scalar quotient maps form cones over both quotient towers: consecutive compatibility follows by functorial sheafification and the representative rule. Naturality therefore proves compatibility with every tower transition. The map q composed with the constant ell quotient is the constant uniformizer quotient, since the two ring homomorphisms send x to its class. Every constant ell quotient is surjective on sections by step 2. Cancel this quotient to deduce both cross-tower commuting squares from scalar naturality. The identity and composite reduction equations follow from the functor laws of the two towers.

proof.text: Let c be the constant-to-completed map. The normalization in sp_completed_coefficient_limit gives c followed by beta_N equal to the constant ell-power quotient. Step 3 then gives c followed by beta_N and q_(N,j) equal to the constant uniformizer quotient. The limit lift defining c gives the same scalar normalization for delta_j. Apply lem-sp-completed-integral-finite-quotient-hom-ext with I equal to the (j+1)st uniformizer ideal; its positive-power hypothesis holds with k=j. This proves beta_N followed by q_(N,j) equals delta_j. The compatibility equations for both completed projection families are the limit cone naturality equations, precomposed by the recorded comparison for the ell tower. This uses no new construction of either completion and is valid for all ramification indices e>=1 and arbitrary T.
